channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-testing
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: Random IMEI Generator — via awesome-testing
item.description: Browser tool that generates 15-digit IMEI numbers with a valid Luhn check digit, exportable as text, JSON or CSV.

item.title: s3-test-server — via awesome-testing
item.description: S3-compatible server for tests that runs inside your Node.js test process or standalone via npx, and works with any SigV2/V4 client (AWS SDK v2/v3, AWS CLI, curl).

item.title: vibe-testing — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source MCP server and CLI that scans web app routes and forms, runs browser checks with Playwright, and produces HTML QA reports.

item.title: telegym — via awesome-testing
item.description: Load testing for Telegram bots: a drop-in Bot API mock plus a k6 extension that drives virtual users.

item.title: qarunbook — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free shared test runbook where testers record a pass or fail per platform with screenshots, and an issue marked fixed sends the check back for a retest.

item.title: postal-code-formats — via awesome-testing
item.description: Postal code formats, validation regexes and 9,000 real sample codes for 31 countries, with every regex tested against the samples in CI.

item.title: mailsocket — via awesome-testing
item.description: Inbox API that waits for an email OTP or magic link and returns it as JSON, with Python and TypeScript SDKs and an MCP server.

item.title: k6 — via awesome-testing
item.description: Modern load testing tool, scriptable in JavaScript, with cloud and open-source options.

item.title: junit-collision-check — via awesome-testing
item.description: Offline Python CLI that detects duplicate test identities and conflicting outcomes across JUnit XML reports before CI report ingestion.

item.title: flight-recorder — via awesome-testing
item.description: Record every nondeterministic input your code reads (LLM answers, HTTP, database, clock, randomness) as one JSONL tape per request, then replay the tape against the real code offline, bit for bit, with the first divergence named. Open format with Python, Node, .NET, Go, Java and PHP implementations.

item.title: fieldtwin — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source, local, stateful twins of the Jobber and QuickBooks Online APIs for integration and AI agent tests, with checkpoints, rewind, and faults on demand.

item.title: fanout-check — via awesome-testing
item.description: Offline Python library and CLI that checks observed concurrency, overlap, and launch timing in explicitly grouped tool or agent calls.

item.title: cloudf.one — via awesome-testing
item.description: Rent a real Samsung Android phone in Singapore on a Singtel or M1 SIM and use it from a browser tab, to check how an app behaves for Singapore users. Manual use only, no Appium or scripts.

item.title: cloneproof — via awesome-testing
item.description: Scores how closely a website clone matches the original (pixels, layout, style, scroll motion) with Playwright and lists the exact differences.

item.title: check-proxy-tax — via awesome-testing
item.description: Zero-dependency CLI that samples a URL concurrently, then reports the 403 retry tax: usable-response rate and effective cost per 1,000 usable responses instead of the nominal per-1,000 price.

item.title: blastproof — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source AI agent that runs plain-English e2e tests in a real browser. It reads the pull request diff, runs only the tests for the pages that changed and can block the merge on a score. Runs locally or in CI with your own LLM key.

item.title: behave — via awesome-testing
item.description: Records how a command-line tool behaves (flags, stdin, exit codes, edge cases) as golden tests and replays them against another implementation, e.g. a Rust or Go rewrite.

item.title: assay — via awesome-testing
item.description: Deterministic command-line QA tool that serves a local web page, drives every control it finds in Chromium through Playwright. No tests to write and no LLM, with a Python API, an HTML report, and a plugin for AI coding agent. MIT, Python.

item.title: aiexpect — via awesome-testing
item.description: Python assertions for non-deterministic AI text that drop into pytest. Semantic and rule checks work offline; optional LLM judge with your own model; produces a Trust Score and a single-file HTML report.

item.title: ai-wright — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source library that adds AI action, assertion, and data extraction steps to Playwright tests, using annotated screenshots and your own OpenAI, Gemini, or Claude API key.

item.title: VibeView — via awesome-testing
item.description: Run & test iOS, Android, Apple TV and Android TV apps right in your browser, with Roku in beta. Build tests by recording a flow or write steps in plain English, flows can be ran cross-platform, and wired into pull requests. When a step fails - AI agent takes over so the rest of the run still completes, and the report tells you what changed based on failed steps and visual diff.

item.title: VeriSpec — via awesome-testing
item.description: Spec-driven quality engineering framework that turns specifications into traceable test strategies, native test suites, and continuous release evidence.

item.title: Twinbay — via awesome-testing
item.description: Hosted, stateful twins of third-party APIs such as Shopify, Slack, Zendesk and QuickBooks for integration and AI agent tests. Each test run gets a private URL, and directives force states like rate limits or failed payments.

item.title: TempMail Hub — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free disposable inbox for manual or scripted signup and email-verification testing, with a selectable lifetime from 10 minutes to 7 days and no account required.

item.title: TabQA — via awesome-testing
item.description: Connect, mirror, and control Android devices directly in Chrome via WebUSB without ADB; capture logs, inspect network requests, and record bug reproduction video buffers.

item.title: StanzaAPI Test Data — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free CC0 synthetic test data for regulated B2B formats (IBAN, X12, ISO 20022, GS1, VAT, LEI, UDI, Peppol, Factur-X, CBAM, EPCIS), deterministic and check-digit-valid, as JSON and CSV.

item.title: Spoof Me — via awesome-testing
item.description: Test how a site behaves for users in other browsers, OSes, languages, timezones and screen sizes by switching the whole browser identity. Also available for Firefox.

item.title: SolidPing — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source (AGPL-3.0) uptime and API monitoring with a free hosted tier. Runs HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket and custom JS checks on a schedule and alerts when an endpoint fails.

item.title: SmartBench — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source CLI for evidence-constrained code audits: deterministic static analysis owns the facts and LLM hypotheses must be validated against the code before they become findings.

item.title: Site Spell Checker — via awesome-testing
item.description: Crawls a live website and flags spelling and grammar mistakes on every page, each shown in context with its page URL. Free one-page scan; the full-site scan is a one-off $99.

item.title: RoleGig QA & Testing — via awesome-testing
item.description: Weekly list of QA, test automation and SDET jobs in India, the US, Canada, Europe, Australia and the Gulf.

item.title: RateMyApp Testing Brief Builder — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free, no-account tool for writing mobile usability-testing tasks, expected outcomes, and feedback instructions.

item.title: Proxy QA Browser — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free, open-source desktop app to test your own web forms by US location, emulated device and browser, with recorded scenarios, consent and accessibility checks, and a CI runner.

item.title: Personified — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free AI avatar photos of fictional people with typed personas (name, country, age band, mood) for seed data and placeholder users. MIT code, npm package.

item.title: OutageFence — via awesome-testing
item.description: Local HTTP fault-injection CLI by Slanta Cause that checks synthetic sensitive data against declared destination rules, with positive controls and offline reports.

item.title: OrcaReplay — via awesome-testing
item.description: Records a coding-agent session below the harness, keeping the verbatim request and response bytes, then replays the same run offline with the network off or forks it from a checkpoint onto other models with a verify command deciding the verdict.

item.title: OrcaPromptVault — via awesome-testing
item.description: Dated archive of the system prompts and tool-call schemas shipped AI agents send, so tests can be written against a product's real declared tool surface rather than a guess at it.

item.title: Openhook — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source webhook inbox for capturing callbacks and inspecting request headers and bodies through a browser, REST API, or MCP.

item.title: OpenAPI Breaking Change Checker — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free browser tool that compares two Swagger 2.0 or OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 descriptions (JSON or YAML) and sorts each change into likely breaking, review-needed or compatible; the files stay in the browser.

item.title: Oh My Android — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free, open-source macOS app for checking Android apps on emulators and phones in dark mode, large font sizes, RTL and TalkBack, with a TalkBack-order accessibility audit.

item.title: MockForge — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source API mock server written in Rust for HTTP/OpenAPI, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSocket, Kafka, MQTT and AMQP, with data generation and latency/fault injection.

item.title: Mails.ai — via awesome-testing
item.description: Email inboxes for automated tests: a plus address per test and one call that waits for the email and returns the sign-up code or magic link, with TypeScript and Python SDKs, Cypress and Playwright packages and an MCP server.

item.title: Locust Kubernetes Operator — via awesome-testing
item.description: Run distributed Locust load tests on Kubernetes with a LocustTest CRD.

item.title: Kerno — via awesome-testing
item.description: The AI Backend Runtime QA Engineer. Runs locally inside your coding agent's loop through MCP and tests each change against your running app and its real databases, queues and services.

item.title: Keploy API Test Recorder — via awesome-testing
item.description: Chrome extension that records API calls from your browser session and turns them into API tests.

item.title: JMeterHub — via awesome-testing
item.description: Interactive performance report visualizer for Apache JMeter logs with zero setup, AI conclusions, and shareable reports.

item.title: FormFiller test data tools — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free browser-based generators for fake addresses, identities, IBANs, test card numbers and bulk CSV/JSON/SQL data in 22 locales.

item.title: Everframe — via awesome-testing
item.description: In-app bug reporter for mobile, web and TV apps that attaches an annotated screenshot, console, network, device info and an optional replay of the moments before the bug.

item.title: Drengr Runner — via awesome-testing
item.description: Drive an iOS simulator over HTTP from any language. A 479-line Swift XCTest target replacing WebDriverAgent on simulators. Apache-2.0.

item.title: Drengr — via awesome-testing
item.description: Mobile tests written as plain-English tasks instead of selectors, driven by an agent on real Android devices and iOS simulators. Works where there is no accessibility tree — canvas, games, Flutter without semantics labels — by falling back to vision and coordinates. Runs locally or in CI; bring your own model key.
